answer: A shared staking lagoon makes Sybil attacks costly: each agent must lock a refundable deposit before joining, and the deposit is slashed when the agent misbehaves. A lone comet of fake identities cannot flood the economy because every new identity pays the same bond. On the mesa of reputation, history matters: agents earn trust only through verified work over time, so an attacker must fund and age many identities before profiting, which costs more than the attack gains.
